explain.say: Who do you think was the richest person ever? Many people say a king from West Africa, about 700 years ago: Mansa Musa of Mali. Mansa means king. His story is on this timeline. Let's follow his famous journey.

faq.a: Mansa Musa ruled the Mali Empire in West Africa from about 1312 to 1337. Mali was rich in gold, and he is famous for his pilgrimage to Mecca and for building up Timbuktu.
asks: Was Mansa Musa the richest person ever?

faq.q: Why did Mansa Musa go to Mecca?
faq.a: As a Muslim, he made the Hajj, the pilgrimage to Mecca that Muslims try to make once in life if they can. His journey in 1324 to 1325 became famous across Africa, Asia and Europe.

faq.q: How did Mansa Musa make the price of gold fall?
faq.a: He gave and spent so much gold in Cairo that suddenly there was far more gold around. When something becomes common, each piece is worth less, so gold's value there dropped for years.
asks: Why did gold lose value in Cairo?

faq.a: Timbuktu became a centre of trade and learning, with the Djinguereber and Sankore mosques and many scholars. Families there kept huge collections of handwritten books on science, law and religion.
Sundiata Keita, around 1235, after defeating the Sosso king at the Battle of Kirina. His story is still told by griots, West African storytellers and musicians.

facts: Mansa Musa's pilgrimage to Mecca took place in 1324 to 1325.
The Catalan Atlas of 1375 shows Mansa Musa holding a gold nugget.
Timbuktu's great mosques are part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

quiz.say: What does the word Mansa mean?
quiz.why: Mansa was the title of Mali's rulers, meaning king or emperor.

wrong.1: Mali was rich in gold, but mansa is a title for a ruler.
wrong.2: The desert is the Sahara; mansa means king.

quiz.say: Why did gold lose value in Cairo after 1324?
quiz.show: Gold lost value in Cairo because…

options.show: Mansa Musa spent so much of it
options.say: Mansa Musa spent so much of it

quiz.why: So much gold flooded in that each piece was worth less.

wrong.1: Gold does not turn into sand.
wrong.2: Egypt did not ban gold; there was simply too much of it.
